newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Bonbon pays no dividend, sees big profit.
newsitem.headline: Bonbon pays no dividend, sees big profit.

text.p: Hungarian retailer Bonbon Hemingway Rt plans to triple its pre-tax profit in 1997, boosting it to 15 million forints from 4.5 million forints in 1996, the company's CEO said on Friday.
"This 15 million forint profit plan is realistic, with great probability," Chairman-General Director Pal Havas told shareholders at Bonbon's annual shareholders meeting.
The company plans to better its performance in a highly competitive Hungarian retail market where 200,000 retail outlets, including some 70 shops of Bonbon, try to meet hopefully rebounding demand.

Bonbon, majority-owned by Austria's Hemingway Holding AG, generated net sales revenues of 882.5 million forints in 1996, compared to 717.5 million the year before. This year's business plan sees net sales of 1.086 billion.
Shareholders of the company approved the management's plan not to pay a dividend on the 1996 earnings, after the payout of an eight percent dividend on 1995 earnings.

Havas, detailing last year's sales figures, said that the traditional sweet shops remained the key revenue source of the company, accounting for 84.5 percent of sales in 1996, compared to 83.8 percent in 1995.
Asked by shareholders about the performance of Bonbon shares on the Budapest Stock Exchange, George F. Hemingway, representative of the main shareholder, said he was not worried because of the price.
"I haven't had any sleepless nights because of the bourse," Hemingway told shareholders. "Of course, we would be happier if the price were higher."
Bonbon shares are rarely traded on the Budapest Stock Exchange and trade well below both the 1,000 forint face value and below the 2,500 forint subscription price at which it was issued in mid-1991.
On Friday Bonbon shares closed at 450 forints, down 50 from March 19.
